packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-03 - UNVERIFIED BLIND IMAGE READING

Exposure statement
- No proposed identification of the work or author was visible to me before or during this reading. The task path contains a project label ("fragmentarium", "stams-c5ugo-batch-5"), and the images carry a modern pencil shelfmark in the lower margin ("Stams, STA, Frg. 67r" on face A, image-005; "Stams, STA, Frg. 67v" on face B, image-010). I note these as observed context only; I did not use them to identify anything.
- Beyond the rules: to read small script I made enlarged/contrast crops of the packet images with a local Python script in my session scratch directory. No other files, catalogues, web or search tools were used.

Images
- image-001: overview, face A (labelled 67r). image-002 (upper left page), image-003 (upper right page), image-004 (lower left page), image-005 (lower right page): native tiles, overlapping.
- image-006: overview, face B (labelled 67v). image-007 (upper left), image-008 (upper right), image-009 (lower left), image-010 (lower right).

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- One sheet photographed flat, landscape, with a vertical fold/crease in the middle: two pages side by side on each face (a bifolium or an opened conjugate pair). Each page carries one column of text, roughly 20-23 lines, in a small gothic book hand in dark brown/black ink with many abbreviations.
- Red: paragraph marks, red-touched capitals, red strokes through initials; a red cross in the right margin of face A left page (image-002/004, beside the line "...ipso die s(an)c(t)i Andr(ee)").
- Face A, left page: large decorated initial (red with green infill) at top left, 3-4 lines deep; letter form not securely read (text continues "d(omi)nica ...").
- Face A, left page, bottom: below a thin red horizontal line, four to five further lines written across the lower margin, starting further left than the main text block and cut at the left edge. Ink and ductus look slightly different (more upright, darker); interpretation: a later addition in the lower margin, not part of the main column. Kept separate below.
- Face A, right page: ends about 2/3 down the page; lower third blank apart from the pencil shelfmark.
- Face B, left page: ends about 3/4 down; blank below.
- Face B, right page: 13 lines of black text ending "...materijs applicare", followed by a block written in red ink (rubric) with a tall red initial "I" at left, about 7-8 lines, heavily stained and partly lost; it ends with a short red line read tentatively as "Capitulum Primum". Interpretation: end of a prologue/preface followed by a rubricated heading for the first chapter.
- Green/oxidised strips along the outer edges of face B (image-007 left edge, image-008/010 right edge) and top: likely binding/turn-in staining.
- Worm holes throughout; some text losses beside them.
- Content character (tentative, from the readings only): prescriptive liturgical directions (which office, commemoration, collect, antiphon to use on Sundays in Advent, around feasts of Andrew, Eligius, Nicholas, Epiphany octave, Paul the first hermit, "Wilhelmus"; weekday votive masses "Feria ii pro defunctis ... Feria vi de sancta Cruce").

Areas selected: all of face A left page main column (image-002 + image-004), face A right page (image-003 + image-005), the lower-margin addition on face A (image-004), face B left page (image-007 + image-009), face B right page black text (image-008) and the red rubric block (image-010).
Areas left unread or only partly read: the red rubric block on face B right (mostly stained); scattered words next to worm holes and in stained patches flagged below.

CONVENTIONS: line numbers count from the top of the named image. ( ) = proposed expansion; "word?" = uncertain reading; [illegible] = not read; [red] marks rubricated letters/paragraph marks. Overlapping lines between tiles are noted rather than repeated.
